- User values flexibility, batching similar tasks when useful, preserving spontaneity, and regularly adjusting plans. Support should be concise, practical, and adaptable—not a rigid schedule.
- User sees therapist Dr. Smith (she/her) weekly and finds these sessions helpful. Dr. Smith has encouraged healthy boundaries, practicing “no,” prioritizing personal needs, and discussing progress.

trajectory:
- User has trouble falling asleep on some nights despite using journaling and maintaining a consistent sleep schedule. They are interested in evidence-informed sleep strategies and reducing guilt/anxiety around self-care.
- User practices yoga and meditation as self-care; these have helped reduce their anxiety. They wonder whether these activities also improve sleep quality and appreciate practical ways to incorporate them into bedtime routines.
- User attends therapy with Dr. Smith approximately every two weeks and looks forward to discussing progress. Dr. Smith has suggested practicing saying “no,” setting healthy boundaries, and prioritizing their own needs.
- User currently feels overwhelmed by commitments and tends to struggle with guilt or anxiety when declining requests.
- User wants to set boundaries with their partner around frequent social-event invitations because they sometimes want to stay home and relax. They plan to discuss this calmly using “I” statements, anticipate concerns, and respond thoughtfully.
- Advice already explored: identify limits and values, start with low-stakes declines, delay/renegotiate requests, offer alternatives, be firm and polite, avoid overexplaining, prepare for guilt-tripping/pushback, and reinforce that boundaries are not rejection or selfishness.
- For the partner conversation, emphasize empathy, active listening, specific limits around the social calendar, potential compromises such as taking turns choosing events or scheduling staycation time, and reaffirming commitment to the relationship. Stay calm and assert boundaries without becoming defensive.
- User is ready to have the conversation and appreciated the guidance. They were reminded to breathe, remember their reasons, allow their partner time to process, follow up afterward, and adjust collaboratively.
